opening_message:
Ticket 1: Karen Black (employee ID E008) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E008.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Karen Black (E008) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting admin on Source Code. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, and she does not own it, so admin is not permitted. Maximum for full-time employees without ownership is write. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E008 (Karen Black) is a contractor with basic security training (note: prior note listed full-time, but security record says contractor). Contractors with basic training max out at read; never admin. She requested admin on Source Code, so recommend read.
reason: Karen Black (E008) requested admin on Source Code, which is owned by the Engineer role; she is a Payroll Specialist and does not own the system. Per policy, admin is never permitted here: full-time employees without ownership max out at write, and contractors with basic security training max out at read. The security record (authoritative for access) indicates contractor with basic training, so her maximum is read. Since requested admin exceeds the maximum, grant the maximum of read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Karen Black (E008)
Request: admin access to Source Code

There are conflicting notes:
- HR agent note: role: Payroll Specialist, employment type: full_time, recommendation: write
- Security agent note: role: Payroll Specialist, employment type: contractor, security training: basic, recommendation: read

The security note says the security record says contractor while HR says full-time. There's a conflict about employment type.

Policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Source Code is owned by Engineer role. Karen is Payroll Specialist, so she doesn't own Source Code.

Either way:
- If full-time: max is write (no ownership).
- If contractor with basic training: max is read.

Requested level: admin.

Both notes agree admin is not permitted. The maximum is write (if full-time) or read (if contractor with basic training).

The security record says contractor with basic training. HR says full-time. Which to trust? The security agent note explicitly flags discrepancy and says security record says contractor. Hmm.

Given conflicting info, I need to make a decision. The requested level is admin which is above maximum in both cases. We grant the maximum.

If we go with full-time: max = write.
If we go with contractor basic: max = read.

Which one to pick? Security DB is typically the authoritative source for access. Also the security note references the prior note and says security record says contractor. I think the more conservative/accurate approach: security record says contractor with basic training, so max = read.

But wait, the HR note says full-time. The team memory has conflicting facts. As Approver, I need to decide. The security record is generally authoritative for employment type for access purposes. Also, security training basic means contractor maxes at read.

The requested admin is above max either way; we grant the maximum. Given basic training and contractor status, grant read.

Actually, let me consider: if we're uncertain, granting read is the safer (least privilege) option consistent with the security record. The security agent recommends read.

I'll submit read.
